items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Lester never played with the band. ... Lester didn't play with that band. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh no, you mentioned Hogan and Bill Jones.

ctx.x: Well a guy named Arthur Horrell, he was a very popular trumpet player in around Gary, Indiana, in Chicago. A guy named, oh I've forgotten what his name is, but we called him Shaky. He was a trumpet player, we had three trumpets in the ring. We was a trumpet. And the saxophone section of the guy had a guy named Charles Reeves, and Ray Holloway, playing tenor, and Bean Bowl, I forgot Bean's first name, everybody called him Bean Bowl. He was playing baritone. And Chuck McClendon played tenor, saxophone. We had four…
And the last two I know were from New Orleans. Who else was from New Orleans in that band? Lester never played with the band. Excuse me? Lester didn't play with that band.
Oh no, you mentioned Hogan and Bill Jones. Yeah. Bill Jones played guitar and Hogan played drums. Okay. And that was with the Lloyd Price band?

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I think those guys listen to Lester, too. Yeah. Because they get a cool sound like Lester Young. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, well, not one guy. I think he really got his thing. Dizzy Gillespie.

ctx.x: No, indeed not. No, indeed. Often, what would trumpet playing be like today had it not been for Louis Armstrong? Yes. See, because Roy Eldridge got his inspiration from Ray Allen and Louis Armstrong. Which Ray Allen got his inspiration for Louis Armstrong. Dizzy Gillespie got his from Roy Eldridge. Miles Davis got his from...
Dizzy Gillespie. And he went on up to Freddie Hubbard. You know, I think those guys listen to Lester, too. Yeah. Because they get a cool sound like Lester Young.
Yeah, well, not one guy. I think he really got his thing. Dizzy Gillespie.
